audit.why: 54.18% over 299 games, EVEN. The read is right and unusually well argued: Camille owns the isolated 1v1 permanently because Swain has no dash, but the grouped fight is genuinely his. Level 1 and level 6 are the flat stages; 2-3 and first item are hers.

Camille's ladder (level 2-3 Hookshot stun, level 6 arena, first-item bruiser peak) and Swain's (Demonic Ascension uptime plus soul stacks at two items) are both stated. Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at every rank, which is worth knowing and now appears.

audit.whatIsWrong: Swain's passive is referred to twice as 'his drain passive' / 'his drain-passive heal' and never named. Camille's R is written without its article throughout.
audit.why: Riot's name is Ravenous Flock, and it is not merely a heal — it is health drain plus damage that scales off the target's maximum health, which is why armour stacking is the wrong answer against him and why the 'his drain passive can't out-sustain a clean stun combo' line is only true before Grievous Wounds is in the picture. _missing-interactions.json flags both the anti-heal requirement and the resistance-invalidation for this exact matchup and neither reaches the page. Nevermove is 12s at rank 1 down to 10s, against Hookshot's 16s — so 'force all-ins while his E is on cooldown' is a shorter window than the text implies and needs the number.
audit.corrected: Ravenous Flock named with its drain and max-health damage; Grievous Wounds cue added; Nevermove's 12s and Demonic Ascension's 120s written in; R given its full name.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Force them while his E is on cooldown' and 'punish his Demonic Ascension cooldown' both name a cooldown without a duration, and the second one names the wrong ability.
audit.why: Nevermove at 12s is the cooldown that gates every trade — it is the root that turns a whiff into a kill. Demonic Ascension at 120s is not something you punish in lane, it is something you avoid extending into.
audit.corrected: Both retimed with real numbers, Nevermove identified as the punishable cooldown.

audit.why: The win condition — use the R to yank Swain out of position before a fight rather than diving past him — is the correct use of a 475-range point-and-click anchor against a dashless drain tank, and it is already stated in late.

edits.before: Swain's whole early threat is Nevermove (E) — the bird that flies out, returns, and roots you into Vision of Empire (W) and Death's Hand (Q) poke. At Level 1 you both have one ability and low damage, so just respect the snare and farm. The instant you hit 2 and 3 you flip it: bait or side-step the E, then Hookshot in, land the second-cast stun, and Q-recast for the true-damage hit. His drain passive can't out-sustain a clean stun combo, and he has no dash to punish your engage once his root is on cooldown.
